caption: The drawing depicts a round ceramic plate viewed from above, featuring a decorative floral design. The plate is primarily tan or beige in color, with the rim adorned by a brown and reddish border that incorporates a repeating leaf-like pattern. Inside, the surface of the plate is decorated with symmetrical arrangements of stylized flowers and leaves in shades of brown, orange, green, and muted purple. Five large flower motifs, each constructed of elongated oval petals with leaf texture, are spaced around the center, connected by delicate, curving stems and smaller floral elements. The year "1822" is written in green numbers near the top center within the design. The composition centers on a larger flower motif with radiating leaves, flanked by smaller flowers and abstract leaf shapes. Scattered around are additional small leaves, buds, and curvilinear flourishes in similar earth-toned colors. The artist’s name "CHARLOTTE ANGUS" is faintly inscribed on the white background outside the plate’s lower right edge. The background surrounding the plate is left plain and uncolored.
title: Pa. German Plate
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
